title: $Lf^*$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of the
setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. The derived pullback

$$
Lf^*\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)
$$

is the restriction of the ambient derived pullback $Lf^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]
to bounded constructible complexes, which it preserves by [lem-sfb-dc-upper-star-preserves]. It
commutes with the inclusions into $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$ and $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$.

proof.text: Write $F=Lf^*$ for the ambient functor of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. For $T=X,Y$, let $P_T$ be the property of being bounded constructible and let $\iota_T$ be the full-subcategory inclusion of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], with coefficients and scheme hypotheses as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. For an object $(K,h_K)$ of $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda)$, define its image to be $(F(K),h_{F(K)})$, where $h_{F(K)}$ is [lem-sfb-dc-upper-star-preserves] applied to $K,h_K$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $\Lambda$ is a commutative condensed ring and $f$ is a morphism of the stated setting; no restriction on the coefficient ring is added.

For a morphism $u:(K,h_K)\to(K^{\prime},h_{K^{\prime}})$, define the restricted map to be $F(u)$. By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], these morphisms are the ambient derived-category morphisms, so $F(u)$ is a morphism between the objects just constructed. The ambient functor of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] satisfies $F(1_K)=1_{F(K)}$ and $F(v\circ u)=F(v)\circ F(u)$; the same equations hold in the full subcategory because its identities and compositions are the ambient ones. This defines the restricted functor.

Under the inclusions of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], the restricted functor sends an object to the ambient $F(K)$ and a morphism to the ambient $F(u)$. Thus both composites $\iota_X\circ (Lf^*|_{D_{\mathrm{cons}}})$ and $F\circ\iota_Y$ have the same object and morphism assignments, establishing the asserted compatibility with inclusions.
